messages:
acme_infra: Heads up — our production webhook started throwing JSON parse errors after the v7b deploy last night. We only saw it once traffic hit peak. stack trace: `JSON.parse` Unexpected token ',' at position 102

acme_infra: Example payload we received (raw body):
```
{"result":[{"id":1,"text":"ok"}],"meta":{}} ,{"result":[{"id":2,"text":"more"}],"meta":{}}
```

acme_infra: That extra `,` between the two JSON objects is breaking our parser. We don't do streaming concat normally — those are single HTTP POSTs from your webhook.

sara_support: ugh, thanks for the report. Can you share the request id + endpoint you hit? also which model/route?

acme_infra: route: `prod-json-mode` using `redwood/llama7b-v7b:2026-03-16`
request id: `req_0a9f4c3b`
endpoint: `https://api.redwood.prod/generate`

ben_eng: thanks — looking. quick question: were you using streaming=true on the client by any chance? or non-streaming?

acme_infra: we are non-streaming. We only saw the single POST body with the concatenated objects (above). No SSE.

ben_eng: weird. sharing a quick log pull for `req_0a9f4c3b` from our edge:
```
[edge] recv chunk 1: "{"result":[{"id":1,"text":"ok"}],"meta":{}}"
[edge] recv chunk 2: " ,{"result":[{"id":2,"text":"more"}],"meta":{}}"
[stream-joiner] concatenated -> "{...}} ,{...}}"
[webhook-forward] POST body sent to customer with raw concatenation
```

ben_eng: it looks like our internal streaming/joiner layer treated two logical generation frames as separate fragments and inserted a joining separator (`,`) when assembling. That would produce exactly the broken payload you pasted.

maria_prod: to be explicit: v7b rollout changed the model tokenization / eos behavior a bit; the runtime's join heuristics might now be mis-detecting completion boundaries and inserting separators for multipart responses.

acme_infra: is there a quick mitigation? we need the webhook healthy; customers are seeing failures.

ben_eng: immediate mitigations: 1) we can force non-stream-join mode for your route (server-side) — that will buffer and send a single JSON (safe). 2) fallback to `redwood/llama7b-v7a` (previous tag) while we patch. 3) if you can, add a tolerant parse wrapper on your side to handle concatenated JSON objects for a short window.

acme_infra: option 1 or 2 would work for us. preference is keep using v7b but without the joiner hack.

maria_prod: noted. I'm putting a canary rollback + joiner-disable for `prod-json-mode` as an emergency config change. deploy-bot will post events.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary config change scheduled: disable-stream-joiner on route `prod-json-mode` (targets: 2 nodes) by maria_prod — starting now.

ben_eng: I'll open an eng-runtime ticket with payloads and the raw chunk dumps. quick root cause hypothesis: joiner uses punctuation-aware boundaries and used `,` as a separator opcode when it saw a model token stream that started with a punctuation-like token. v7b introduced a tokenization sequence that emits an extra leading comma token for some finish sequences -> joiner misinterprets and injects a literal comma between fragments.

ben_eng: repro steps for eng-runtime: reproduce with `--model=redwood/llama7b-v7b:2026-03-16` and `--structured-output=true` on high batch sizes; examine `stream-frame` output around EOS. I'll attach the exact request we used.

acme_infra: thanks, appreciate the quick triage. please ping when canary is done. :pray:

sara_support: confirming — canary applied to 2 nodes, monitoring for 5m. I'll update once we see clean webhooks. :eyes:

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary change applied (nodes: n2, n7). health checks passing.

acme_infra: receiving normal single JSON again. parser errors gone. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

ben_eng: followup action items: - eng-runtime to add a regression test for joiner not inserting separators between consecutive top-level objects - add a canary gate for models with changed EOS tokenization - patch joiner to avoid inserting punctuation separators outside JSON strings

maria_prod: opened internal issue IR-2026-348; assigned to eng-runtime. tagging for a hotfix in next 48h.

sara_support: closing this thread when fix lands or we confirm stable for 24h. leaving open for now.

acme_infra: will monitor and report if anything else crops up. thanks again!
